note: Findings from the Chapter 12 system validation. Severity is the author's assessment, not an audit rating. Safe reproduction cases use synthetic data only.

findings.invariant: Saved, signed, confirmed, indexed and active are shown as separate readings; a failed server call is not shown as success.
findings.reproduction: Create an account and vault, expire every auth_sessions row in the test database, then create a matter. The vault reports 'Not signed in. Sign in to your account first' and 'Unsaved changes', but the header Server sign-in reading still says 'Signed in' until the next sign-in or sign-out.
findings.result: No unauthorised access: the save is refused, the draft is kept and no session is silently created. The stale reading is a presentation inconsistency.
findings.remaining: Update the Server sign-in reading when a protected route answers 401, with a regression test.

findings.invariant: Consent is bound to exactly what the reviewer selected; consent is renewed when the disclosure changes.
findings.reproduction: Select a passage and choose Explain (a preview appears), then select a different passage and press Send without choosing Explain again. Send transmitted the FIRST passage, which the preview identifies only by page and length.
findings.result: setSelection now discards a preview that was built under a different selection ('The selection changed, so the preview was discarded. Nothing was sent.'). Regression: controller.test.ts 'discards a preview when the selection changes' and the system privacy spec, which confirms only the newly consented excerpt reaches the provider.
findings.remaining: None for this case. The preview still names an excerpt by page and size, not by its text.

findings.invariant: Renewing an expired fee quote re-quotes the same unsent operation and needs a new confirmation; it never strands the account.
findings.reproduction: Sign the approval, wait 30 seconds without pressing Send, then press Renew quote. The controller created a NEW reservation for an account that still held the earlier quoted operation (one unresolved operation per account), so the server answered ACCOUNT_BUSY and the panel showed 'Not sent'. The only way forward was waiting out the five-minute unsigned lease. The controller test used a fake API that had no such limit, so it passed.
findings.result: requote now asks the same operation for a fresh quote and falls back to a new reservation only if that quote is refused. Nothing is re-signed or sent by renewal. Regression: controller.test.ts (two tests) and the system spec, which waits out a real 30-second quote, renews, and sends exactly one transaction.

findings.invariant: A confirmed block that a later reading contradicts is reported as a contradiction, never as a second confirmation on another block.
findings.reproduction: Confirm an operation, then refresh while the node reports the receipt under a different block hash. The stored record was protected (a confirmed row never changes), but the refresh response described the new reading as a plain confirmation with no mismatch, because the remembered block hash was never passed to the monitor.
findings.result: reconcileOperation passes the stored block hash as previouslyConfirmedBlockHash for a confirmed operation, so the observation is 'unknown' with mismatch CONTRADICTS_CONFIRMED while the stored confirmation neither moves nor disappears. Regression: the system case 'a changed block hash after confirmation'.
findings.remaining: The browser panel's presentation of a contradicting observation is not separately tested here.

findings.invariant: After the verifier has loaded, local verification needs no network.
findings.reproduction: Open the standalone verifier, cut the network completely, then choose a file. The worker script is fetched on first use, not at page load: the request was aborted (net::ERR_ABORTED) and no result panel appeared within 30 s. What the page displayed was not captured. After one check while online, the script comes from the HTTP cache and a fully offline check works.
findings.result: No disclosure and no wrong result: the check simply does not run. The test serves hashed assets with long-lived cache headers (as a static host would), warms the worker with one online check, then goes fully offline.
findings.remaining: Decide whether the verifier should fetch (or inline) its worker at load so first use works offline, and what the page should say when the worker cannot start. Hosting with cache headers is not yet decided.

findings.invariant: No fake listening or speaking state: the page never claims a state the engine has not entered.
findings.reproduction: Press Play before the speech engine fires its start event: the page said 'Speaking'. Press the microphone while recognition was still starting: the control said 'Listening'.
findings.result: Read-aloud has a 'starting' playback state (counted as active for Stop) and says 'Speaking' only after the engine's own start event. The microphone control says 'Starting… press to cancel' until recognition starts. Unit test in voice.test.ts and the voice-local-speech system cases cover it.
findings.remaining: Speech objects in the system tests are scripted stand-ins; real OS/browser engine timing is unproven.

findings.invariant: Refusals, errors and Stop warnings (including a possibly-sent transaction) are readable at 320 CSS px.
findings.reproduction: At 320 and 390 px the command dock clamped its status line to one row, so a refusal or a Stop warning could be cut off. Seen in the 320 px screenshots.
findings.result: The one-line clamp now applies only to the idle hint (no Stop note and no notice). A regression check types 'approve' at 390 and 320 px and asserts the notice is not clipped.
findings.remaining: None known for the tested notices. Automated checks cover tested controls only, not WCAG certification.

findings.invariant: Voice capability must not break the page when speech is unavailable or unusual.
findings.reproduction: In headless Chromium 153 in this sandbox, SpeechRecognition.available({ processLocally: true }) crashed the renderer (standalone Playwright probe against a localhost page). With the voice flag on and no stand-in, the page died at load.
findings.result: The system tests install speech stand-ins and hide the real objects for the 'unsupported' case, so the suite does not exercise the real call. Real-device behaviour is unknown.
findings.remaining: Query capability lazily on first use of the control rather than at load, and check on a real device in task 15.

findings.reproduction: Open the disclosure preview and press Escape: it stays open. It sends nothing and has its own Cancel button.
findings.result: No change made; Escape confirmed nothing in any tested dialog or drawer.
findings.remaining: Decide whether Escape should close the preview, for consistency with the drawers.

findings.invariant: The configured chain endpoint is the only endpoint: no redirect substitutes another host.
findings.reproduction: Start the production build with the chain endpoint set to a loopback server that answers every request with a 307 to a second loopback server, then read /api/chain/status. The second server received the JSON-RPC POST bodies (3 requests).
findings.result: The viem HTTP transport now sets fetchOptions redirect 'error', as the SDK RPC clients, the Envio client and the Qwen client already did. The same case now shows the redirector asked and the redirect target never contacted; the status is 'unknown' with RPC_UNAVAILABLE.
findings.remaining: The endpoint is operator configuration, so exploitation needs a compromised or misconfigured provider. The case uses loopback servers, not Alchemy.

findings.invariant: A hostile document never reaches a string-to-code path in the page.
findings.reproduction: Run the PDF import in the production build and listen for securitypolicyviolation events.
findings.result: pdf.js is now opened with isEvalSupported false in both getDocument calls, so PDF function streams are interpreted rather than compiled with eval. This is hardening: the installed pdfjs-dist is past the fix for the eval-related arbitrary-code advisory CVE-2024-4367, and the test did not find the extractor itself raising a violation.
findings.remaining: None known. Rendering and extraction of the synthetic PDFs still pass.

findings.invariant: A legitimate feature raises no Content Security Policy violation, so a real violation is not lost in noise.
findings.reproduction: Open any page of the production build with a securitypolicyviolation listener: one script-src 'eval' report per page load, from zod's JIT capability probe (Function('') inside a try/catch).
findings.result: A nonced script, public/zod-jitless.js, sets zod's global jitless option before any bundle runs. Parsing still works through zod's interpreted path. Account, vault and PDF-worker flows now raise zero violations. The policy was not loosened.
findings.remaining: Relies on zod's __zod_globalConfig global; a zod upgrade must keep the case green.

findings.invariant: No reachable high or critical vulnerability remains unresolved.
findings.module: indexer (envio and its pinned transitive dependencies)
findings.reproduction: pnpm audit --prod: 14 advisories (5 high, 2 moderate, 7 low) in express 4.19.2, body-parser, path-to-regexp, qs, send, serve-static, cookie, ws and esbuild, all under indexer>envio.
findings.result: Envio pins express 4.19.2 exactly, and its newest release (3.14.1) still does, so pnpm-workspace.yaml now overrides only the vulnerable ranges to patched versions (express 4.22.3, body-parser 1.20.8, path-to-regexp 0.1.13, qs 6.16.0, send 0.19.2, serve-static 1.16.3, cookie 0.7.2, ws 8.22.0, esbuild 0.28.2). pnpm audit --prod now reports no known vulnerability; the lockfile changed only for those packages. The indexer config check, 31 indexer tests and envio codegen still run. None of these packages is in the web, verifier or package bundles.
findings.remaining: The Envio runtime itself is not exercised here, so the patched express under it is untested at run time. Remove the overrides when envio ships fixed versions. The audit needs network access; offline it is blocked, not clean.

findings.invariant: The standalone verifier cannot be framed by another origin.
findings.reproduction: The verifier's Content-Security-Policy is a <meta> element. frame-ancestors is ignored in a <meta> policy, so the page itself cannot refuse framing.
findings.result: The meta policy was checked: default-src none, script-src self, connect-src only itself and the listed registry origins, object-src, base-uri and form-action none.
findings.remaining: Framing protection must come from host response headers (frame-ancestors and X-Frame-Options). Hosting is not decided; this is a Chapter 13 check.

findings.invariant: State what the page policy does and does not stop.
findings.reproduction: Under 'strict-dynamic', a script element created by already-trusted script runs without a nonce. Injected markup in the server's HTML (unnonced script, inline handler, eval) is blocked; script created by first-party or dependency code is not.
findings.result: No change. This matches the comment in proxy.ts: the policy limits injection and does not isolate unlocked material from same-origin code.
findings.remaining: No claim of protection against a compromised dependency or DOM-based injection by first-party code.

findings.reproduction: GET a route that exports only POST (for example /api/assistant/runs): the framework answers 405 with an empty body and no Cache-Control.
findings.result: No data in the response; every other tested page and API response, signed in and out, carried no-store.
findings.remaining: Optionally add Cache-Control: no-store to framework-generated 405s through the header rules.

findings.invariant: No committed or committable file holds a credential.
findings.reproduction: pnpm secrets:check reports KEY_ASSIGNMENT and PROVIDER_KEY_URL in the git-ignored local .env. It also read tests/system/harness/harness.test.ts (deliberate credential-bearing database URLs) and, for minified build output, mistook `https://host\",...ox@` for a URL credential.
findings.result: Committable files (tracked and untracked-not-ignored) and both build outputs are clean by shape, and planted secrets are detected. The harness test is allowlisted with a reason, as the other deliberate invalid-input tests are. Build output is scanned with the stricter asset-scanner shapes, not the source scanner.
findings.remaining: secrets:check still fails on the real, git-ignored .env, so the secret-scan readiness check stays failing. Decide whether the scanner skips ignored files or the values move; do not commit .env.
